messages.author: Qinghua Liao
messages.body:
Hello,
I used Amber/Orca/Plumed to do QM/MM metadynamics simulations to study a
chemical reaction,
but I found that the substrate, which was treated with QM method, was
twisted unphysically, as attached.
In the attached figure, the carboxylate and hydroxyl groups on the sugar
ring are twisted, even the benzene ring are open.
But none of the bond breaking is related to the chemical reaction.
Similar problem was also observed when I used DFTB3 as QM method.
Even the artifacts happened during the simulation, the simulation was
not crashed, but went on. Does someone also have similar problem?
What is the possible reason for the unexpected issues? Any comment is
appreciated!
All the best,
Qinghua

....dac

messages.author: Qinghua Liao
messages.body:
Hello David,
Thanks a lot for your reply! I followed what you suggested.
I turned off plumed by setting plumed = 0, but I saw the same kind
of twisting of molecule during the simulation.
What possible problem could lead to such unphysical twisting?
Any other suggestions? Thanks so much!
All the best,
Qinghua

messages.author: Goetz, Andreas
messages.body:
> On Nov 21, 2020, at 3:32 PM, Qinghua Liao <scorpio.liao.gmail.
com> wrote:
>
> I turned off plumed by setting plumed = 0, but I saw the same kind
> of twisting of molecule during the simulation.
>
> What possible problem could lead to such unphysical twisting?
What you observe could be due to a bad starting structure or a system that was not minimized / equilibrated, thus resulting in unphysically large forces that break the molecule.
How did you prepare the system before switching to QM/MM?
How does your starting structure look like?
All the best,
Andy
